findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:239 — Darkening notification badge backgrounds while retaining $secondary text reduces black-theme 11px counter contrast to approximately 2.46:1, making counts difficult to read.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — The light-theme branch changes reply-author lightness from 30% to 70%, washing out author links even though this fix should preserve light-theme colors.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:239 — Darkening notification badge backgrounds while retaining $secondary text reduces black-theme 11px counter contrast to approximately 2.46:1, making counts difficult to read.

adjudication.rationale: The diff at line 239 in badges.css.scss shows the change from `background-color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `background-color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The finding correctly identifies that in dark themes, this creates a darker background (30% lightness of $secondary) while the text color remains $secondary (as shown in the unchanged `&[href] { color: $secondary; }` on line 240-241). This would indeed create poor contrast - a dark background with light text where both are derived from $secondary could result in low contrast ratios. The specific contrast ratio of 2.46:1 cannot be verified from the diff alone, but the accessibility concern about reduced contrast is valid and grounded in the actual code change.
